items.t: Tata Motors Raises Iveco Stake To 96.29%, Plans Squeeze-Out
Tata Motors subsidiary’s tender offer for Iveco Group shares nears 96.29%
sum: TML CV Holdings B.V., a subsidiary of Tata Motors, has reported provisional results from the reopening of its voluntary tender offer for all common shares of Iveco Group N.V. The offeror has now reached a shareholding of approximately 96.29% of Iveco Group’s common share capital, excluding treasury shares. The payment date for shares tendered during this period is set for November 13, 2026.

Tata Motors Limited, through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary TML CV Holdings B.V. (formerly TML Commercial Vehicles Limited), has announced the provisional results of the reopening of its voluntary totalitarian tender offer for all common shares of Iveco Group N.V. The company informed the exchanges on November 7, 2026, that TML CV Holdings B.V. has received these provisional results from BNP Paribas, the intermediary responsible for coordinating the offer.
- Shares Tendered in Reopening: 18,309,029 common shares were tendered during the reopening of the terms, representing approximately 6.75% of the Issuer’s common share capital.

- Aggregate Shareholding: With these new acceptances, and considering shares already tendered, the Offeror has reached a provisional shareholding of approximately 96.29% of Iveco Group’s common share capital, net of treasury shares. This figure includes the 238,157,212 shares tendered during the initial acceptance period (approx. 87.81%) and 4,868,597 treasury shares (approx. 1.80%).
- Total Countervalue: The aggregate value for shares tendered during the reopening amounts to EUR 263,650,017.60.
- Payment Date: The payment for shares accepted during the reopening of the terms is scheduled for November 13, 2026.

Given the provisional results, which, if confirmed, would bring the Offeror’s aggregate shareholding to at least 95% of the Issuer’s issued and outstanding share capital, TML CV Holdings B.V. intends to commence the Dutch Legal Squeeze-Out procedure for the remaining outstanding common shares. This may be preceded by a demerger and share sale at the Offeror’s discretion. Borsa Italiana will suspend trading and/or delist the shares in accordance with regulations.

Tata Motors stock gains 8% as Iveco synergy hopes rise
sum: Tata Motors shares gained 8% in Thursday trading, according to Business Today. The November 5 report focused on the potential benefits of Tata Motors' completed Iveco acquisition and on the execution risks that could shape the recovery in profitability.

Nomura said the transaction could create integration benefits through cost efficiencies and sourcing advantages. It maintained a target of Rs 511 and said the pace of cost optimisation and earnings recovery would remain important monitorables.

HSBC retained its Buy rating with a target of Rs 500. Business Today reported that the 12-month consensus target stood at Rs 503, based on 25 recommendations, while the brokerage range cited in the report extended from Rs 416 to Rs 645.

The analyst view also points to pressure inside Iveco. European commercial-vehicle demand remains uneven, and Nomura said Iveco's industrial margin fell to zero in the third quarter of calendar 2026. The report said a gradual improvement in profitability was expected over 2028 and 2029, although execution remains central to that outlook.

Nuvama said Tata Motors was broadening its electric-vehicle pipeline across small commercial vehicles and trucks. The brokerage also pointed to growing electric-bus and electric-truck adoption, supported by government policy and rising customer acceptance.

Tata Motors is a mobility group developing products and services around sustainable fuels, technology and materials, according to its investor information. Its commercial-vehicle operations cover the Indian market and, through Iveco, extend into European trucks and buses. The group is also expanding its electric-vehicle offering across commercial-vehicle categories.

items.t: Iveco Acquisition: Tata Sons Chairman Chandrasekaran Meets Italian PM, Shares Company's Strategy
sum: On October 30, Tata Motors said it has acquired an 89.42 per cent stake in Iveco for nearly 3.43 billion euros.

New Delhi: Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran has met Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni at Palazzo Chigi in Rome, with the acquisition of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco Group by Tata Motors featuring prominently in discussions amid growing strategic industrial and economic ties between the two countries.

Sources said Chandrasekaran presented the Tata Group's strategy following the Indian conglomerate's acquisition of a controlling stake in Iveco Group, one of Italy's leading commercial vehicle manufacturers, at the meeting held on Wednesday.
The meeting came amid the increasing strategic economic and industrial collaboration between Italy and India.

Addressing a global press conference at Iveco's headquarters in Turin, Italy, on Tuesday, Chandrasekaran thanked the Italian government and Prime Minister Meloni for their encouragement and support throughout the acquisition process.

"Iveco Group, with very strong Italian roots and a strong presence across Europe and Latin America, brings huge industrial heritage, iconic brands, technology and world-class capabilities across trucks, buses and power trains.

"I would like to thank everyone who has been involved in this transaction, and I'm grateful to all of them. I would also like to start today by thanking the Italian government and the Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and Minister Adolfo Urso for their encouragement and support throughout this process," the Tata Sons Chairman said.

sum: Razorpay has received Sebi approval for a proposed ₹5,000 crore to ₹6,000 crore IPO, marking a key step towards a public listing. The company is targeting the January-March quarter of 2027, but the final timing will depend on market conditions and investor demand.

Razorpay has taken a significant step towards joining India’s public markets after securing regulatory clearance for its planned initial public offering, according to a report by Times of India. The Bengaluru-based digital payments company is preparing for a fund raise in the ₹5,000 crore to ₹6,000 crore range, even as the exact launch window will hinge on market sentiment and investor appetite.Regulatory approval opens the doorSecurities and Exchange Board of India has given its nod to the proposed issue, people familiar with the matter told the publication. That approval does not lock in a launch date, but it does remove a key regulatory hurdle for one of India’s best-known fintech names as it weighs the timing of a public listing.Razorpay’s scale, Sebi clearance is often the most visible signal that the long road to an IPO is entering a more concrete phase. sum: Tata Motors plans local assembly of Iveco vehicles, eyes global expansion
Chandrasekaran sees scope for component sourcing and taking Tata products overseas as the combined Tata Motors-Iveco group targets higher volumes, revenue and margins over five years

Tata Motors is exploring the local assembly of select Iveco Group vehicles in India, initially through the semi-knocked-down (SKD) route, as the two companies begin identifying opportunities to introduce products across each other's markets following the Indian automaker's acquisition of an 89.42 per cent stake in the European commercial vehicle major for approximately €3.4 billion.

Speaking at a global press conference in Turin, Italy, on Tuesday, Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran said the companies had complementary product portfolios, creating opportunities for growth in India and overseas markets.

Responding to a Business Standard question on whether India could emerge as a manufacturing or component sourcing hub for Iveco's global operations, Chandrasekaran said: “There are specific products of Iveco Group, which will have a lot of relevance in India. And we are already identifying those products. Obviously, those products will have to be localised in India, at least to start with in a semi knockdown manufacturing.” He added that Tata Motors' products and platforms could also be introduced in markets where Iveco has an established presence. “Obviously, there are opportunities in the areas of components, batteries and many other areas. These are things to be worked on,” he said.

The press conference, attended by journalists from several countries in person and through a live stream, came days after Tata Motors acquired the controlling stake in Iveco through the initial settlement of its tender offer on October 30, bringing the Italian-headquartered company under its control.

The acquisition has created the world's fourth-largest commercial vehicle manufacturer by truck sales volumes in the above-six-tonne segment, with annual revenue of approximately €21 billion and combined sales volumes of around 590,000 vehicles. The group operates in more than 130 countries, with 27 manufacturing sites, 25 research and development centres and over 73,000 employees.

Massive surge! Reliance Industries shares up 12% after Q2; add ₹2 lakh cr in mcap — when did RIL last rally this much?
sum: Reliance Industries shares surged nearly 12% to ₹1,300 on Monday, their biggest comparable daily gain since April 2020, after the company reported record second-quarter profit. The rally added ₹1.84 lakh crore to its market value, lifting it to ₹17.6 lakh crore.

The shares finished Monday’s trade with a solid 12% jump to settle at ₹1,300 on NSE, their highest level since early September. The stock last posted a comparable single-day surge in April 2020. Given its heavyweight status in the Nifty 50, the rally also lifted the index by 1.7%, even as tensions in West Asia remained elevated.

For long-term Reliance Industries shareholders, the sharp rise has revived confidence in the stock, which had been trending lower since the start of 2026. The shares closed in the red in eight of the previous 10 months. Despite Monday’s rebound, the stock remains down 17.22% so far this year.

The double-digit jump in the stock added ₹1.84 lakh crore to the company’s market capitalisation, taking it to ₹17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India’s most valuable listed company.

At its peak of ₹1,611, the company commanded a market capitalisation of ₹21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the ₹21 lakh crore mark in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve this milestone.

Meanwhile, investors in the Reliance Group have another reason to celebrate, as its telecom arm, Jio Platforms, made a blockbuster stock market debut last week, listing at ₹1,440 apiece, a premium of 21.3% over its issue price.

Reliance Industries Ltd reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹29,550 crore for the July-September quarter (Q2 FY27), marking a 33.8% increase from ₹22,092 crore in the year-ago period. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record ₹62,409 crore.

Jio Platforms vs Bharti Airtel shares: Which telecom stock to buy after Reliance arm’s IPO listing? Experts suggestions
sum: Jio Platforms’ strong market debut has intensified comparisons with Bharti Airtel. Experts view Jio as a higher-growth bet on 5G and digital services, but warn its valuation is demanding. Airtel offers stronger earnings visibility, cash flows and capital discipline.

The listing of Jio Platforms has put the spotlight on India’s telecom sector, with investors now weighing whether the newly listed Reliance Industries-backed company or established rival Bharti Airtel offers a better investment opportunity.

Jio Platforms shares have surged nearly 28% from their issue price of ₹1,119 since making their market debut on Wednesday, 28 October, taking its market capitalisation to nearly ₹13.18 lakh crore and making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. The strong debut and subsequent gains follow an IPO that attracted bids for 22.19 times the shares on offer.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, has built a strong long-term track record, with its shares delivering returns of 586.10% over the past decade and 187.07% over five years. However, the stock remains down 6.64% so far in 2026. With Jio commanding a substantial valuation and Airtel offering an established earnings track record, which telecom stock should investors consider now? Experts weigh in on their growth prospects, valuations and investment appeal.

Bharti Airtel, meanwhile, remains a stronger proposition for investors seeking earnings visibility, higher ARPU, robust cash flows and disciplined capital allocation. Experts say investors should weigh valuations, earnings growth and execution risks before choosing between the two telecom stocks.

Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Jio’s listing at a valuation of around ₹10.3 lakh crore places it among India’s top five companies by market capitalisation from day one. This, he said, changes the investment question from assessing the company’s growth potential to evaluating the returns investors can realistically expect from current levels. Companies of this scale rarely grow significantly faster than the broader economy, making low double-digit annual returns a reasonable base case.
He also noted that ARPU growth in India has historically been uneven, with increases largely coming through tariff hikes in 2019, 2021 and 2024.
